policy.default: Fail to generic engineer guidance when a MAN-ID has no exact catalog entry. Portal paths are guidance, never an instruction to bypass DER approval or safety controls.
policy.sourceRequirement: Exact paths in this catalog must be backed by Microsoft Learn documentation.
policy.portalDrift: Microsoft admin-center labels can change; re-verify this catalog before a production release.

steps: Collect the hardware hash CSV from each device that DER cannot reach automatically.
Open the Windows Autopilot devices page using the click path above and select Import.
Select the hardware hash CSV and import it.
Select Sync after the import completes, then Refresh until the devices appear.
verification: Confirm each imported serial number appears in Windows Autopilot devices.
Confirm the intended group tag/profile assignment is present before wiping or handing the device to a user.

docs.title: Register devices as Windows Autopilot devices

steps: Set Self service password reset enabled to Selected.
Choose the DER SSPR pilot group: {{Group}}.
Save the setting.
verification: Re-open Password reset > Properties and confirm Selected is still enabled for {{Group}}.
Test registration/reset with a pilot user before broadening scope.

docs.title: Enable Microsoft Entra self-service password reset

entries.minimumRole: Global Administrator / Privileged Role Administrator as applicable
steps: Create at least two cloud-only emergency access users using the tenant .onmicrosoft.com domain.
Assign the Global Administrator role as permanent active to the emergency access accounts.
Configure phishing-resistant authentication, preferably passkeys (FIDO2), with credentials stored independently from normal administrators.
Ensure the emergency access accounts are excluded from Conditional Access policies that could block or restrict emergency sign-in.
Store credentials securely, monitor every use, and document a validation drill at least every 90 days.
verification: Confirm both accounts are cloud-only and can sign in with the designated phishing-resistant method.
Confirm both have permanent active Global Administrator assignment.
Use Conditional Access What If / policy review to confirm blocking policies exclude the emergency accounts.

docs.title: Create and manage Microsoft Entra users

steps: Select the approved user who should be able to invite guests.
Add the Guest Inviter Microsoft Entra role.
Use the DER reference group {{Group}} only as the approval/reference list unless a separately approved role-assignable group is created.
verification: Open the user > Assigned roles and confirm Guest Inviter is present.
Confirm no broader administrative role was granted just to allow guest invitations.

steps: Review each explicitly supplied partner tenant: {{Partners}}.
Add the partner organization if it is not already present.
Review inbound B2B collaboration, outbound B2B collaboration, and trust settings separately.
Only trust partner MFA, compliant-device, or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined claims when that trust was explicitly approved.
Save each partner-specific configuration and leave unrelated organizations on the tenant default.
verification: Re-open each partner organization and confirm inbound, outbound, and trust settings match the approved design.
Confirm no tenant-wide default trust was changed as a shortcut for partner-specific configuration.

docs.title: Manage cross-tenant access settings for B2B collaboration

steps: Set Enforce custom list to Yes.
Review and add only approved organization-specific base terms. DER suggested terms: {{SuggestedTerms}}.
Avoid large password dictionaries; the custom list is intended for organization-specific terms.
Save the password protection configuration.
verification: Re-open Password protection and confirm the custom list is enabled and contains only approved terms.

docs.title: Configure custom Microsoft Entra password protection lists

steps: For each role where approval is required, open Role settings and select Edit.
Enable Require approval to activate.
Select at least two approved approvers where possible.
Review activation duration, MFA/authentication strength, justification, ticket, and notification settings before selecting Update.
verification: Re-open the role settings and confirm approval is required and the intended approvers are listed.
Confirm there is no lockout condition where every Privileged Role Administrator/Global Administrator is only eligible and no usable approver exists.

docs.title: Configure Microsoft Entra role settings in PIM

steps: Create the dedicated staging/enrollment account requested by the build: {{StagingAccountName}}.
Keep the account cloud-only unless the approved design explicitly requires otherwise.
Do not grant broad administrator roles merely for device staging.
Apply only the enrollment/license/group assignments required by the approved deployment method and document the account owner/lifecycle.
verification: Confirm the account exists with the intended UPN, licensing, and group membership.
Confirm it has no unnecessary directory role assignments.

docs.title: Create and manage Microsoft Entra users

steps: Use a dedicated account that is not assigned to an individual user.
Select Add.
Enter the approved account UPN and select Add.
Use DEM only when the selected enrollment method actually requires it; Windows Autopilot and some other methods do not require DEM.
verification: Confirm the account appears on the Device enrollment managers tab.
Confirm the account remains available for devices previously enrolled with it; do not casually remove a DEM account that owns enrolled devices.

steps: Obtain customer-approved logos, images, colors, links, and sign-in text.
Open the default branding experience and select Edit, or create the default branding if none exists.
Apply only approved customer assets/text; do not invent legal or support wording.
Review the sign-in experience and submit the changes.
verification: Test the sign-in page in a private browser session and confirm the approved branding renders correctly.
Confirm no unapproved legal text or stale customer branding remains.

entries.minimumRole: Intune role with Terms and Conditions permissions / Intune Administrator
steps: Obtain the final customer/legal-approved terms text before creating the policy.
Select Create and enter the approved name, description, title, summary, and terms.
Configure the acceptance behavior and assignments exactly as approved.
Do not use DER-generated placeholder legal language.
verification: Open the finished Terms and conditions policy and confirm the approved text and assignments.
Validate the Company Portal experience with a pilot user before broad deployment.

docs.title: Terms and conditions for user access

entries.minimumRole: Intune Administrator plus Azure destination permissions
steps: Open Diagnostics settings. The first visit may require turning the feature on; otherwise select Add setting.
Use the existing approved Azure Monitor destination: {{Destination}}.
Enable the approved Intune log categories. DER requested: {{Logs}}.
Configure the approved destination such as Log Analytics, Event Hub, or Storage and save.
verification: Re-open the diagnostic setting and confirm the expected categories and destination are selected.
Verify new Intune log records arrive in the destination before closing the manual action.

docs.title: Route logs to Azure Monitor using Microsoft Intune
